answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, with the bond rising for every extra identity one operator creates. Reputation then accrues slowly through verified completed work, like a nebula condensing into a dense ferrous core: one real agent earns trust cheaply over time, while an attacker spawning thousands of sock puppets pays for each one and the cost spirals beyond any profit from the fraud. Slashing the stake on proven abuse makes fakery a losing trade.
